what_failed_and_why.multi_mechanism_failure_mode: Multi-mechanism (size-selective + hydrodynamic) was proposed as the universal retention solution. The V21 Pareto verdict 'pareto=true for all payloads' was based on a flawed metric (conc=0.0 for all at 90 days) and did not properly compare multi against the BEST SINGLE mechanism per payload. CORRECT analysis: multi is Pareto-OPTIMAL for antibody (0.55 retention at 90% drain vs 0.488 at 95% for size_sel alone), but Pareto-DOMINATED by hydrodynamic alone for peptide/small_molecule (hydro: 0.484 at 92% vs multi: 0.376 at 90%). The multi-mechanism ADDS flow resistance (drain 90% vs 92%) WITHOUT improving retention for small payloads (0.376 vs 0.484). Multi is engineering complexity without retention benefit for 2 of 3 payload classes.
what_failed_and_why.hydrodynamic_alone_failure_mode: Hydrodynamic alone is payload-agnostic — it slows drainage for ALL payloads (drug and water) uniformly. Therefore it is NOT 'selective' retention. It fails T4 (selectivity ratio = 1.0). Cannot be patented as 'selective retention' — would be a generic flow-restriction valve, anticipated by EnClear US12337140B2 (external CSF circuit with flow control).
what_failed_and_why.size_selective_alone_failure_mode: Size-selective filter alone is SELECTIVE (T4 passes for antibody, ratio=488x) but ONLY works for large payloads (above MWCO 30kDa). For peptide (5kDa) and small_molecule (500Da), retention = 0 — fails T1. Also fails T3 robustness for antibody at 90th-percentile worst-case (high fouling drives ret_eff to 0). Also fails long-duration durability (1 year: retention drops to 0 due to membrane degradation).
what_failed_and_why.mechanical_valve_failure_mode: Mechanical valve (close valve during drug delivery) is payload-agnostic (like hydrodynamic) — fails T4. Also fails T3 robustness and T5 Pareto (dominated by hydrodynamic alone which has better drainage).
what_failed_and_why.fundamental_physical_limitation: The 'selective retention of ALL therapeutic classes' is a fundamental physical contradiction. CSF water (18Da) must pass through any size-selective filter that allows drainage. Any payload SMALLER than water (none, but small molecules 500Da are only 28x larger) cannot be selectively retained by size alone. Affinity-based retention (A2) is the ONLY mechanism that could plausibly retain small molecules selectively — but it requires a payload-specific binding partner (one matrix per therapeutic). There is no universal 'selective retention' architecture for small payloads.

size_selective_filtration_for_large_ther.scope: Acute (≤90 day) retention of LARGE THERAPEUTICS (≥30kDa: antibody 150kDa, scAAV9 gene vector ~5MDa, nanoparticles 100nm ~10MDa) at NOMINAL patient conditions
size_selective_filtration_for_large_ther.performance_at_nominal_90day: 0.488 retention (49% of initial therapeutic concentration), 95% drainage preserved — passes T1 (≥0.30) and T2 (≥0.85) and T4 (selective) and T5 (Pareto-optimal for antibody)
limitations: FAILS T3 robustness: at 90th-percentile worst-case patient variability (high CSF production × high fouling × high protein), retention drops to 0 due to membrane fouling
FAILS long-duration durability: at 1 year, retention = 0 due to membrane degradation. Chronic implant lifespan (5+ years per engineering blueprint) is NOT achievable.
FAILS for peptide (5kDa) and small_molecule (500Da): cannot retain below MWCO
Membrane fouling drives ICP risk: per FOULING_ICP_SIMULATION.json, 50% fouling = minimum acceptable drainage (5 mL/hr), 90% fouling = CRITICAL ICP risk (30 mmHg pressure drop)
size_selective_filtration_for_large_ther.patentability_assessment: Patentable as a NARROW sub-invention: 'Size-selective filtration membrane for ACUTE retention of LARGE therapeutic agents (≥30kDa) in CSF drainage shunts.' 102 SURVIVES per corrected 102_MATRIX.json (no single reference has all 6 limitations). 103 UNCERTAIN for Combo 3 (CereVasc delivery + generic filtration) — MODERATE motivation but functional interaction.
size_selective_filtration_for_large_ther.buyer_value: REDUCED — acute large-therapeutic retention is a niche application (gene therapy vectors, antibody therapy). Does NOT solve the universal 'selective retention' problem the territory was scoped to solve.
size_selective_filtration_for_large_ther.recommended_action: PRESERVE as patentable sub-invention. Document as 'CEREVASC_INVENTION_002_PARTIAL_SURVIVOR_LARGE_THERAPEUTIC_ACUTE' if CEO chooses to file. NOT a continuation of #2 — separates from the multi-mechanism negative ceiling.

v_next_opportunity_identified_not_author.mechanism: Therapeutic agent binds to a matrix within the eShunt, preventing it from draining with the CSF fluid. eShunt's one-way valve allows CSF fluid to drain while the matrix retains the therapeutic agent.
v_next_opportunity_identified_not_author.why_this_could_succeed_where_multi_faile: Affinity-based retention is payload-size-INDEPENDENT. As long as a binding partner (aptamer, antibody, molecularly-imprinted polymer) can be designed for the therapeutic, ANY payload size (including small molecules 500Da) can be selectively retained while water drains.
v_next_opportunity_identified_not_author.engineering_cost: Per-therapeutic binding matrix design. Each new therapeutic requires its own matrix development (weeks-to-months per therapeutic). NOT a one-size-fits-all solution.
v_next_opportunity_identified_not_author.prior_art_risk: UNKNOWN — V8.2 search did NOT specifically target affinity-based retention in CSF shunts. Combo 3 risk applies (CereVasc delivery + known affinity matrices from drug-delivery literature).
